newsitem.title: UK: IPE futures trade slightly lower, looking to NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE futures trade slightly lower, looking to NYMEX.

text.p: IPE June Brent futures maintained a downward course on Thursday amid lingering bearish sentiment over crude oversupply and U.S. inventory data, brokers said.

June Brent was at 1357 GMT trading 10 cents down at $17.71 a barrel, having earlier slipped to an intra-day low of $1766 a barrel. May gas oil traded down $1 a tonne at $161.75 following its morning drop of 50 cents from Wednesday's close.
Brokers said the overall market tone remained bearish after publication of American Petroleum Institute (API) weekly data showing a larger than expected build in crude stocks.

Some brokers said the market would wait to see what impact the news of a gas leak overnight at Tosco Corp's 104,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery in Rodeo, California, which forced the company to scale back throughput at some units, would have on the market.
"That leak may certainly help the market this afternoon but I think in general the market is and has been for a while pretty bearish," a broker said.
"We have all these crudes going to the U.S. and I don't think the APIs helped the market at all," she added.

Industry and government data showed U.S. stocks of crude, middle distillates and gasoline all rose last week and the American Petroleum Institute said on Wednesday gasoline supply should more than match peak driving season demand this summer.
Brokers said the largely moderate-volume London market would be looking for direction from NYMEX.
"There's been some pretty good selling in Brent this morning but the market has taken it quite well, so yes, they would be looking for direction on that," she added.
She said that while the market was more likely to move lower, it could go sideways and even move up "but it depends how much impact this gasoline leak that Tosco had" would have on the market.
A second broker said the market was looking for support for Brent at about $17.80.

"We just haven't got the impetus to take us any lower. That will happen when the States come in, I think they may try to up a little bit then push it a lot lower, so I think the next support for us is $17.55 then below that $17.22," he said. Brokers earlier said that the weakness in Brent would pull gas oil lower. Gas oil dipped on the back of Brent's late losses on Wednesday, when the June contract lost 33 cents to close at $17.81 a barrel. GNI energy brokers said heating oil demand in the northeastern United States will rise for the next few days due to cold weather conditions, the worst of which is expected to last until Saturday.
"Therefore, the nearby spreads against crude and gasoline could benefit in heating oil's favour," GNI added in its daily energy report. - Haitham Haddadin, London newsroom +44 171 542 8145
